summary: GitHub watches deduplicate unchanged check results across observations and restarts, distinguish Actions reruns by run and attempt, and label cancelled checks accurately.

replay.detail: No replay changes. Existing observation facts and persisted message subjects provide deduplication.

schema.detail: No new claim fields, tables, indexes or store version changes.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Check wake identity uses the head, producer-selected aggregate state, sorted failed names and counted workflow (run ID, attempt) pairs, excluding raw display checks, readiness and suite metadata. Foreign-app checks and superseded suites do not affect identity. Changes preserving aggregate state, failed names and attempts (such as success to skipped) intentionally do not wake. No-ID checks include commit statuses, non-workflow third-party apps (possibly Mergemaster depending on its reporting), and Actions runs whose databaseId is null: identical recurring results at the same head remain suppressed. Existing observation-key messages remain readable; upgrade may send at most one extra wake for an unchanged result, then persisted result keys deduplicate repeats. Watches distinguish cancelled while github.event retains checks-failed and cancelled required checks retain active refresh cadence. Optional checks remain excluded when required-check rules are available.

recovery.detail: An older build restores observation-based wake identity and treats cancellation as failure; previously delivered messages are retained.
